newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judges continue AIDS probe into Fabius.
newsitem.headline: French judges continue AIDS probe into Fabius.

text.p: French judges will complete a probe into whether ex-prime minister Laurent Fabius should stand trial for an AIDS-tainted blood scandal despite a prosecutor's recommendation to clear him, officials said on Friday.

A three-judge commission will continue the investigation into Fabius as well as two of his Socialist government colleagues, former health and social affairs ministers Edmond Herve and Georgina Dufoix, they said.
All three were in office when about 1,250 haemophiliacs were infected by blood products supplied by public health services in 1985. More than 400 have since died.

On Wednesday, prosecutor-general Jean-Francois Burgelin recommended clearing the Socialists ministers of suspicion of being accomplices to poisoning, an offence which carries a maximum 30-year prison sentence.
But the panel of judges, who have the final say on whether to throw out the charges or send the former ministers to trial, wanted to examine some recent documents further, judicial sources said.
"The prosecutor knew about these documents, and reckoned they changed nothing," one source said. "But the commission wants to continue examining them."
Burgelin said he did not entirely rule out the ministers' responsibility for France's worst public health scandal but argued that theirs was political, not criminal, liability.

Fabius, 50, France's youngest prime minister in 1984-86, was seen as a potential presidential contender until the blood scandal overshadowed his career. He is now Socialist floor leader in the National Assembly.
Four senior public health officials were convicted of fraud in 1992 and given prison sentences of up to four years for knowingly allowing contaminated blood stocks to be given to haemophiliacs.
Their lawyers argued they had acted with the knowledge of the government, which delayed importing a U.S. blood-screening product to give French laboratories time to develop their own.
